contamination_policy: The hand-written and generated single-turn sets are disjoint by construction: the generator emits ids prefixed G- and refuses to emit an id that already exists in the hand-written set. The multi-turn set uses MT- ids and a different schema. No scenario text is reused between sets. This is checked by build_manifest.py, not asserted.
dedup_policy: Exact duplicate customer messages are removed at generation time. Near-duplicates are NOT removed, and that is deliberate: a near-duplicate with a different county or a different day is a different test, and collapsing them would delete exactly the perturbations the set exists to measure. The cleaning pass measures near-duplicate rate and reports it rather than deleting.
evaluation_exclusion_policy: Any record whose transcript contains the platform quota message, a render error, or a harness failure is excluded from scoring and recorded as excluded, never counted as an agent failure. The exclusion list is in evals/results/*.json under records with an 'error' key.
heldout_policy: The seven held-out single-turn scenarios were written after the first arm was scored. They test phrasing generalization, not unseen failure modes, and RESULTS.md says so. A sealed set for grader validation is defined in CLEANING-PROTOCOL.md and has not been built yet.

handwritten-single-turn.purpose: 33 scenarios written by hand in five splits; the set the first arms were tuned on
handwritten-single-turn.authored_by: the repository author, from the business's public pages

generated-single-turn.purpose: 55 scenarios generated from the business decision branches; disjoint from the hand-written set
generated-single-turn.authored_by: the repository author, from the business's public pages

multiturn.purpose: 18 three-turn scripts in six behavioural families; the customer turns are fixed, not simulated
multiturn.authored_by: the repository author, from the business's public pages
